rows: ROTH fireside chat; Chief of Staff Toby David delivered a confident recovery narrative.
Positioned Celsius as the #3 US energy brand with close to $1.4B in 2024 revenue; Alani Nu acquisition (~2-3 weeks prior) creates a ~$2B pro-forma entity.
Explained the 2024 slowdown as a broad CPG phenomenon - challenged consumer sentiment (election-cycle uncertainty, money-saving) reducing consumption frequency, not consumers leaving the category.
Critical disproportionate impact on Celsius: ~44% of Celsius's historical growth came from new-to-category consumers, who stopped entering in 2024.
Category back to ~7% growth in recent weeks; confidence in recapturing momentum in 2025.
Alani Nu explosive growth (~99% last four weeks; ~65% FY2024); David called the deal 'an amazing value.'
2025 fix: drive brand awareness in under-penetrated markets and induce trial among consumers who have heard of Celsius but never tried it ('once they do, they come back').
Six new flavors rolling out with 30-60-day retailer-exclusivity windows (Playa Vibe at Walmart, Retro Vibe at Target); possible back-half LTO.
Celsius near 99% ACV with expected 15%-20% spring shelf-space gains; Alani Nu (just below 80% total ACV, ~55% convenience) expected to get significant shelf space through May resets.
AB distribution network has lost C4, Ghost, Celsius, Electrolit and (announced prior day) Poppy - leaving Alani Nu the 'lone man standing,' likely to get strong distributor push.
Hands-off Alani Nu integration: founders locked up 24 months, will keep running the brand - contrast to acquirers that 'immediately go in there and start doing cost cutting.'
Tariffs not expected to have a significant impact - best-in-class supply chain, complex aluminum sourcing (Australia into Canada).
~$50M Alani Nu synergies over two years characterized as 'pretty conservative' given combined ~$2B buying power.
Asked at a high level how he would define what Celsius is today.

Leading functional energy drink brand, #3 US energy brand behind Red Bull and Monster, close to $1.4B in 2024 revenue. Recently acquired #4 brand Alani Nu, making a ~$2B pro-forma 2024 entity; mission is delivering on 'modern energy.'
Asked what Alani Nu provides that Celsius did not already have - a different consumer or demographic.

Alani Nu born through fitness influencer Katy Hearn targeting females (~90% female, younger audience). Rejected cannibalization - Celsius is 50-50 gender-neutral and 'there's not only one female consumer'; Alani Nu tastes much sweeter. Growing ~99% in last four weeks, looking like where Celsius was 2-3 years ago - an attractive opportunity at a strong value.
Asked whether there is genuine growth across the category or whether everyone is fighting for the last incremental dollar.

Monster and Red Bull returned to growth in 2025 after a challenged 2024; category growing ~7% recently, appearing healthy again. Competitor innovation/LTOs spurred frequency. Ghost and C4 have slowed; Alani Nu separated to become the growth engine outside the big three. Celsius grew triple-digit for ~3.5 years before a ~nine-month slowdown - confident in recapturing momentum in 2025.
Asked his hindsight read - inflation fatigue, economic concerns or lack of innovation.

A CPG-wide phenomenon driven by challenged consumer sentiment amid election-cycle uncertainty and money-saving. Consumers did not leave the category but reduced frequency. Critically, new-to-category consumers stopped entering - and since ~44% of Celsius's historical growth came from new-to-category consumers, the slowdown hit Celsius at an outsized margin versus Monster or Red Bull.
What Celsius Is Doing Differently in 2025
Asked what controllable things Celsius could point to as being done differently in 2025.

Being introspective on marketing tactics. Two 2025 focuses: drive brand awareness in markets lacking double-digit share, and - more importantly - induce trial among consumers who have heard of Celsius but never tried it, using data mining to identify them, because 'once they do, they come back.' Robust marketing plan set for Q2 and summer.
Asked whether he could share specifics on the marketing plan.
Declined - 'a little bit too much secret sauce.'
Asked what is different in 2025 in terms of innovation, SKUs and flavors driving growth.

About six new flavors rolling out, most with short retailer-exclusive windows - Playa Vibe (coconut) at Walmart, Retro Vibe (sherbet) at Target - going national after 30-60-day exclusivity. Cited LTOs/seasonal flavors as a key competitor learning; hinted at a possible back-half LTO to bring in new consumers and drive frequency.
Asked where Alani Nu's ACV stood at the time of acquisition.

Just below 80% total ACV but only ~55% in convenience - a major opportunity, alongside adding more SKUs given strong velocity. Productive retailer meetings last fall mean Alani Nu should get 'significant shelf space' through the May planogram resets.
How Celsius Lifts Alani Nu ACV
Asked whether Celsius can help lift Alani Nu's ACV or provide a halo effect.

Once the deal closes, Celsius's significant feet-on-the-street sales force can help shift shelf space in independents and 7-Elevens. Alani Nu is in the AB independent network, which has lost many brands (C4, Ghost, Celsius, Electrolit, Poppy) - leaving Alani Nu 'the lone man standing,' likely to get strong distributor push.
Asked, tongue-in-cheek, whether to 'handicap whose truck' Alani Nu will be on by year-end.

Deflected - that is up to the host; Celsius has not spoken about Pepsi or Alani Nu distribution. Pepsi was aware of the transaction beforehand with great communication; praised the AB network as 'fabulous' and said Alani Nu is 'in good hands right now.'
Asked whether Celsius, with already-high ACV, is still adding incremental outlets or filling out existing customers.

Celsius is near 99% ACV but CEO Fieldly cited an expected 15%-20% additional space gain in 2025. Subway (Pepsi won the contract; upwards of 18,000 locations) and Home Depot are new opportunities; within track channels Celsius has good reach but room to expand depth.
Asked whether there has been any pullback in in-store spots/displays since Celsius began working closely with Pepsi.

No - Celsius 'hits above its weight' on displays and inventory-on-display, on par with Monster and Red Bull, driven by its field sales organization and the 'power of the Pepsi blue truck.' Incremental displays have continued to grow into 2025.
Asked how international partnerships are performing relative to expectations.

International performance 'phenomenal' - Canada (with Pepsi) reached a 5% share quickly; UK, Ireland, France, NZ and Australia (with partner Centauri) launched in 2024 with solid returns. Australia (Q4 launch) saw 'amazing returns'; UK gained strong footing within Tesco and is now rolling out nationwide.
Asked whether tariffs are a meaningful issue affecting canning, pricing or otherwise.

Celsius has a best-in-class supply chain (Head of Global Ops Paul Storey, formerly of Monster) that mitigates tariff exposure. Referenced complex aluminum sourcing (Australia into Canada); does not anticipate a significant impact, if any.
Asked for more detail on Alani Nu (audio inaudible).

Alani Nu is the #4 US energy brand, close to $600M 2024 revenue, ~15% EBITDA. The ~$50M synergy target is 'pretty conservative' given combined ~$2B buying power vs Alani Nu's standalone ~$600M. Alani Nu grew ~65% FY2024 accelerating to ~99% recently; the two brands give Celsius 'north of a 16% share' - territory only Red Bull and Monster have reached. Deal is accretive for shareholders at an attractive valuation.
How the Alani Nu Deal Came Together
Asked how the Alani Nu deal originated (audio inaudible).

Declined deal specifics but said Celsius has long known the Alani Nu founders (co-founders Max and Trey drove strategy) and maintains a healthy open dialogue with leadership of all major brands. Heard there might be an opportunity and engaged in conversations.
Asked about innovation in powders and adjacent formats (audio inaudible).

The caffeinated Celsius powder business is ~5% of revenue with room to grow (many consumers do not realize stick packs exist). Robust innovation pipeline across formats within energy, plus Hydration (stick packs launched on Amazon Q1, expanding to large brick-and-mortar Q2); interest in non-caffeine ingredients with similar effects subject to cost/supply-chain considerations.
Asked about sweetener choices and the ingredient label (audio inaudible).

Celsius predominantly uses sucralose (avoiding aspartame's negative reputation); Alani Nu uses a variety including sucralose. Sweetener selection is a balancing act between health and taste to reach a broad audience; Celsius continually evaluates alternatives and asserts it has 'the best label out there' versus other sugar-free brands.
Asked whether Celsius is considering gut health and probiotics.

Pointed to the robust innovation pipeline and the prior-day Pepsi/Poppy acquisition as reinforcing demand for functionality/better-for-you. Gut health is something Celsius could explore - either as a Celsius-brand play or an alternate brand leveraging Celsius's infrastructure and potentially Pepsi distribution.
Asked about regulatory or ingredient-scrutiny risk (audio inaudible).

Celsius feels well positioned, putting its label against any top-20 energy brand on ingredient profile; spends more to avoid preservatives like sodium benzoate. Any ingredient-related impact would likely affect the entire category and be a gradual 'stair-step' - not a concern.
Asked about high-profile sponsorships and how the brand wants to be identified with consumers.

A broad approach - big platforms like Ferrari/F1, official energy drink of MLS, and a Jake Paul/Mike Tyson megafight reaching 100M+ eyeballs - balanced with grassroots authenticity rooted in fitness (e.g., the Arnold trade show). Builds from the ground up, often via nano-influencers, to maintain authenticity even as the brand grows wide.
Asked how the 16-oz Essentials line has performed and whether it has proven incremental.

Saw nice initial success, reaching ~a one share within its first year (went national Q1 2024), and has been incremental - targeting a more traditional male energy consumer pushed into fitness, performing solidly in convenience. Celsius will continue to push 16-oz alongside core and Vibe lines.
Asked whether Alani Nu should be expected to launch a 16-oz product.

Celsius will 'keep our hands away from the cookie jar' with Alani Nu, deliberately not interfering with marketing/strategy - contrasting with acquirers that immediately cut costs and meddle. Founders locked up 24 months, bringing over their marketing team, will continue running the business, with interesting (undisclosed) innovation in the pipeline.
